India Urges G20 to Prioritize Diplomacy Over Military Solutions Amid Global Tensions

01 Nov 2026, 11:43 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.amarujala.com

2 min read

Overview of the G20 Ministerial Discussions

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addressed the G20 Foreign Ministers in Atlanta, emphasizing that global crises cannot be resolved through military intervention. Representing India, Jaishankar advocated for prioritizing diplomacy and adherence to international law to address ongoing geopolitical conflicts, including the war in Ukraine and instability in West Asia.

Key Issues Addressed by India

During the plenary session, Minister Jaishankar highlighted several critical areas requiring international cooperation:

  • Maritime Security: He emphasized the need to protect freedom of navigation, citing the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). He noted that attacks on civilian vessels disproportionately burden Global South nations by disrupting the supply of fuel, food, and fertilizers.
  • Industrial Rights: Jaishankar expressed concern over practices that deprive nations of their right to industrial development, such as market flooding, the weaponization of supply chains, and the artificial restriction of market access.
  • Counter-Terrorism: He warned that states must not ignore the threat of terrorism for perceived strategic gains, describing such negligence as a high-risk activity with inevitable consequences for the perpetrators.
  • Resilient Connectivity: The Minister called for the creation of alternative, robust supply chain and connectivity routes to mitigate risks during times of global disruption.

US Perspective and Global Context

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who hosted the event, described the current international landscape as a "time for decisions." Rubio highlighted that G20 nations are facing interconnected economic and geopolitical crises that threaten the foundations of the global economic system, including energy and food security.

Future Engagements

The G20 meeting in Atlanta serves as a precursor to upcoming high-level dialogues. Minister Jaishankar is scheduled to participate in a Quad foreign ministers' meeting with counterparts from the U.S., Japan, and Australia. Following his commitments in the U.S., he is slated to attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda.

Verification

Readers interested in official summaries or specific policy statements from this meeting can verify details through the official portals of the Ministry of External Affairs of India or the U.S. Department of State press briefings.
